text: A big worker survey found blood pressure dropped 11 points, but only among people who cut back on salt.
Coffee seemed to give sleep-deprived students a small memory boost on one word test.
Remote work sped up three startups' software teams, but the benefit vanished within half a year.
Buses over the new bridge saved riders about twenty minutes on average, compared with the roadworks year.
Vitamin D might ward off colds, but one supplement-funded winter study only showed it in kids under five.
A reading app helped young English learners, but the gains faded by the following school year.
Pesticide exposure in one season left bumblebee colonies with about a quarter fewer queens.
Icelandic offices tried a four-day week: burnout fell, pay held steady, and sick days stayed the same.
